display: Graham, retired maths and woodwork teacher who now coordinates a community Men's Shed in Melbourne's northern suburbs. We have a new woodworking program starting in November and an empty 90 m² workshop space at the back.

signals.text: We need a qualified cabinetmaker with an Australian Cert III in Cabinet Making to supervise our council-funded woodworking program, running November to January.
I have sixty members who can build a bookshelf, but none of them holds the certificate the grant asks for.
I'm looking for someone who can turn experienced tradesmen's skills into a formal Cert III, for example through recognition of prior learning.
I'd like to know whether a supervisor could qualify by some route other than holding the paper themselves, and who could confirm that with the council.
The back half of our building has sat empty for months. I'd love to put a proper bench and a few vices in there, but we have no plan or money for it.
I'm worried the program will fall over before it starts and the grant will be withdrawn.
The Shed's finances are fragile. We run on a weekly sausage sizzle and small grants, and there's no money for wages.
I want to take six weeks off from February to travel to Queensland with my wife, so someone has to be able to run the program without me.
Some of our members are lonely or low, and I'd like more ways for them to come in and feel useful without it feeling like a clinic.
I need to find an insurer or broker who understands community workshops, because our cover only applies when heavy tools are used under supervision.
I'm a bit stretched. Between the Shed and the grant paperwork I keep getting home late and I'd like to give my family more of my evenings.
The council grant agreement is signed on 6 October. I have about four weeks to find a supervisor before the November start.

offers.text: Thirty-one years of teaching maths and woodwork in Coburg and Preston, including running classrooms and working with apprentices and beginners.
A brick building in Preston with a main workshop, a small kitchen and a meeting room, available to community programs that fit the Shed.
About 90 m² of empty space with a concrete floor and a roller door, which could suit a small workshop, a co-op or a community maker group.
A funded woodworking program, with a $38,000 council grant, that pairs retirees with apprentices from November to January.
A network of about sixty members whose skills include plumbing, electrical work, veterinary work, banking and violin making. They are happy to mentor, fix things and help with practical problems.
A working relationship with the council's community development officer and experience writing and managing small community grants.
Experience keeping a volunteer organisation running for years on sausage sizzles, grants and patience, including running about $600 a month of fundraising at Bunnings.
A newsletter that reaches Shed members and local supporters, which I can use to spread a call for help.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm a qualified cabinetmaker with a Cert III. I'm semi-retired and would like to supervise a community program a few days a week for a few months.
catchers.can: Offer the supervisor role for the November to January woodworking program, and talk through hours, insurance and any honorarium the grant allows.
catchers.confirm: Do you currently hold an Australian Cert III in Cabinet Making (or a higher cabinetmaking qualification) and can you be on site as supervisor from November to January?

catchers.hypo: I run a training organisation that does recognition of prior learning for trades. I could assess experienced woodworkers who never got the certificate.
catchers.can: Connect me with RPL assessment for the retired tradesmen Frank knows, so that one of them can qualify as supervisor in time or after the program starts.
catchers.confirm: Are you a registered training organisation that can issue a Cert III in Cabinet Making, and could an assessment finish within a few weeks?

catchers.hypo: I teach cabinetmaking at TAFE and I'm looking for community placements for my students and for ways to spread my hours.
catchers.can: Explore a TAFE teacher acting as supervisor of record, with apprentices and retirees working alongside them.
catchers.confirm: Are you a licensed instructor who holds the Cert III and is allowed to supervise outside your TAFE campus?

catchers.hypo: I work in grants at a council or a funding body and have seen supervisor requirements changed or reinterpreted when the program stays safe and fits the intent.
catchers.can: Help me make a case to Priya at the council for a flexible reading, for example a Cert III holder supervising on part of the days with a trained deputy the rest of the time.
catchers.confirm: Have you personally seen a council or funder accept a different arrangement for a supervisor qualification in a grant agreement?

catchers.hypo: We're a small group of makers, repairers or a bike co-op looking for about 90 square metres of space with a concrete floor and a roller door.
catchers.can: Offer the empty back half of the Shed building as a shared workshop and agree what we each bring.
catchers.confirm: Is your group a non-profit or community group that would take on part of the cost of the space and carry its own insurance?

catchers.hypo: My husband retired a year ago and has gone quiet. He used to be good with his hands and I don't know where he could go.
catchers.can: Invite him along on a Tuesday morning, with a cup of tea and a job to do. My wife Lorraine, a retired nurse, and I can also point the family to better support if he needs it.
catchers.confirm: Is he living in the northern Melbourne area, and would he be willing to come along himself on one morning?

catchers.hypo: I'm a retired nurse or counsellor who wants to help men's wellbeing groups and has some time each week.
catchers.can: Link you with Lorraine, my wife and a retired nurse, and with our committee, to talk about gentle wellbeing support at the Shed.
catchers.confirm: Do you hold current health or counselling credentials, and are you offering to volunteer in person in northern Melbourne?

catchers.hypo: I work in insurance for community or volunteer organisations and could look at cover for a workshop that uses heavy tools with supervision.
catchers.can: Review our current policy and what a supervised apprenticeship program would need, and talk through options.
catchers.confirm: Do you advise community or not-for-profit groups in Victoria on public liability or volunteer cover for workshops?

catchers.hypo: I'm a retiree with a good bench vice or two, and some workshop tools I would like to see used rather than sit in a garage.
catchers.can: Take donated benches, vices and tools for the empty back half, and tell you which things are most needed.
catchers.confirm: Are the items in good working order and can you deliver them to Preston, or can someone collect them?

catchers.hypo: I've run a Men's Shed or community workshop and I'd be happy to cover the coordinator's role for a few weeks while the coordinator is away.
catchers.can: Share the Shed's routines and take on a six-week cover from February, so I can travel to Queensland.
catchers.confirm: Have you coordinated a Men's Shed or a similar volunteer workshop before, and are you free for six weeks from February 2027?

forbids.text: I won't put someone in as supervisor who lacks the required qualification, or hide that from the council; the grant conditions are firm and I want to keep the council's trust.
The Shed's budget cannot cover wages, so any paid role needs separate funding that has been agreed in advance.
Our insurance only covers heavy tools when they are used under supervision, so I won't run unsupervised sessions.
The woodworking program has to run November to January, and I can't move those dates.
I will not share members' personal details, stories or health situations with outsiders.
I'm away in Queensland for six weeks from February 2027, and I won't be available then.
I can only handle in-person work around northern Melbourne; I can't take on anything that needs me elsewhere.

projects.name: Back half of the Shed
projects.text: About 90 m² of empty workshop space with a concrete floor and a roller door that I'd like to turn into a proper bench area with vices, or share with a community group.
roles_needed: Community group or co-op wanting workshop space
Donor of benches, vices and tools

policy.t1: When there is a real lead, I'll share the grant conditions, the certificate requirement, the November to January schedule and the supervision rules for heavy tools.
policy.t2: Once the match is clear and I trust the person, I'll talk openly about the Shed's fragile finances and the general wellbeing needs of the men who come.
policy.never: I won't give out any member's personal details, health information or private stories, and I won't pass on my family's private information.
